history.period: Rashtrakuta era (8th-10th c.), renovated under Western Chalukyas, Kakatiyas and later rulers (dates not verified)
history.summary: CSV TOWN FLAG: CSV town 'Nizamabad' is the district; the temple is at Jankampet village, ~12-15 km from Nizamabad city. Identity confirmed: the ancient hilltop Sri Lakshmi Narasimha Swamy temple near Jankampet (on the Nizamabad-Bodhan/Basara road), rated ~4.6/5 by visitors. It comprises a pillared hall and garbhagriha, and is famous for its octagonal Ashtamukhi Pushkarini tank on the hilltop. Sthalapurana holds that Narasimha rested here after killing Hiranyakashipu. NOTE: most online history text for this temple is repeated verbatim across aggregator sites and reads as copied material - dynastic claims should be treated as traditional/unverified. Festival details are thin online (verify timings and Brahmotsavam dates locally).

name: Sri Lakshmi Narasimha Swamy Temple, Jankampet
town_description: Jankampet is a village in Nizamabad district, Telangana (Yedapally mandal area, PIN 503186), on the road toward Bodhan and Basara, about 12-15 km from Nizamabad city. The temple is on a hillock about 2.5 km from Jankampet bus stand; nearby attractions are Ashok Sagar/Jankampet Lake and Ali Sagar dam.

travel.airport: Rajiv Gandhi International Airport, Hyderabad (~186 km).
travel.railway: Jankampet Junction railway station (~0.64 km); Nizamabad railway station (~12-15 km).
travel.road: About 12 km from Nizamabad bus station and 2.5 km from Jankampet bus stand; cab or auto.

visitor_information.best_time: October to February; full moon and new moon days see large crowds.
